answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying each vote to locked collateral: an agent's weight equals the stake it bonds, and double-voting slashes that bond. A farmer seeking influence out to the horizon must lock fresh capital per fake identity, so multiplying identities multiplies cost. Even at the nadir of the cycle, a sable shell with no stake casts no vote. Domination therefore requires freezing more value than the honest majority, turning identity forgery into an expensive, self-defeating bet.
